decisions.reason: The source confirms that the footer is shared and that website pages retain the dark theme, but the candidate's existing same-message Event already establishes the shared footer. The separate page-theme Requirement governs its visual theme without changing the footer's own state.
The landing-page visual direction already specifies a dark theme. Retaining that theme across website pages does not change this candidate's existing landing-page state.
The decision to retain a dark website theme does not alter the plain HTML and Tailwind CSS build stack.
The shared dark theme does not change the landing page's section order, copy plan, How It Works sequence, or sequence visual.
Retaining the dark theme does not change the requirement for responsive landing-page layout.
The website theme decision does not alter which hero text is emphasized.
The dark-theme decision does not change the requirement for a landing-page sign-up button.
The source applies the retained dark theme to website pages, while the dashboard shell remains a separate styling-guidance requirement supporting both light and dark modes.
Responsive breakpoint guidance is addressed by a separate clause and existing same-message Event; the page-theme change does not modify that guidance.
